subject: maths
title: Multiplication
seo_title: Year 5 Multiplication Worksheets: Short and Long Multiplication, Mental Methods
standard_text: Multiply numbers up to 4 digits by a one- or two-digit number using a formal written method, including long multiplication for two-digit numbers; multiply and divide numbers mentally drawing upon known facts; solve problems involving multiplication and division, including scaling by simple fractions and problems involving simple rates.
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on multiplication: mental methods from known facts, short multiplication of 4-digit numbers, long multiplication by 2-digit numbers, missing digits, and word problems with rates and scaling. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Multiply by one digit at a time. For a 2-digit number, make two rows and start row 2 with a place-holder zero.
key_sub: 38 × 24 = 38 × 4 + 38 × 20 = 152 + 760 = 912. Use known facts for mental work: 60 × 7 is 6 × 7 = 42 tens = 420.
body_html:
Mental multiplication: use facts you know

Many big multiplications are a times table fact in disguise. 60 is 6 tens, so 60 × 7 is 6 × 7 = 42 tens = 420.

Other quick ways: change the order (25 × 7 × 4 = 25 × 4 × 7 = 100 × 7 = 700), double and halve (16 × 25 = 8 × 50 = 400), and × 5 is × 10, then halve (46 × 5 = 460 ÷ 2 = 230).

Short multiplication: up to 4 digits × 1 digit

Line up the ones. Start with the ones column. When a product is 10 or more, write the ones digit and exchange the tens into the next column as a small digit. Multiply first, then add the exchanged digit.

Long multiplication: × a 2-digit number

Make one row for each digit. Row 1 multiplies by the ones digit. Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it starts with a place-holder zero (green). Then add the two rows.

3-digit × 2-digit

243 × 36 = ?

Row 1: 243 × 6 = 1,458. Row 2: write 0, then 243 × 3 = 729, so 7,290. Add: 1,458 + 7,290 = 8,748. Check: 243 × 36 is about 200 × 40 = 8,000.

Answer: 8,748

Rates and scaling

A rate is an amount for each one: £12 an hour for 15 hours is 15 × £12 = £180. Scaling means making something a number of times bigger: a jug that holds 6 times as much as a 250 ml glass holds 250 × 6 = 1,500 ml.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Losing or adding a zero (60 × 7 = 42 or 4,200)60 is 6 tens: 6 × 7 = 42 tens = 420
No place-holder zero (38 × 24 = 152 + 76 = 228)Row 2 is × 20, so write 0 first: 760
Forgetting an exchanged digit (38 × 4 = 122)Write it small and add it: 3 × 4 + 3 = 15, so 152
Adding the exchanged digit firstMultiply first, then add: 3 × 4 + 3 = 15, not (3 + 3) × 4
Multiplying by only one digit (38 × 24 = 152)Make a row for the ones and a row for the tens

faq.q: What multiplication do Year 5 children learn?
faq.a: They multiply numbers up to 4 digits by a one-digit number with short multiplication, and by a two-digit number with long multiplication. They also multiply mentally using known facts, such as 60 × 7 = 420.

faq.q: How do you teach long multiplication in Year 5?
faq.a: Start with 2-digit × 2-digit. Multiply by the ones digit to make row 1, write a place-holder zero and multiply by the tens digit to make row 2, then add the rows: 38 × 24 = 152 + 760 = 912.

faq.q: What is the difference between short and long multiplication?
faq.a: Short multiplication is for multiplying by a one-digit number and gives one row. Long multiplication is for a two-digit number: you make one row for each digit and then add the rows.

faq.q: Why do you put a zero in long multiplication?
faq.a: In 38 × 24 the 2 means 2 tens, so row 2 is 38 × 20, not 38 × 2. The place-holder zero in the ones column makes the row 760 instead of 76.

items.q: What is 30 × 400?
items.e: Use 3 × 4 = 12, then put back all 3 zeros (one in 30, two in 400): 30 × 400 = 12,000.
24 is double 12, so 24 × 7 is double 84 = 168.

items.q: What is 5 × 17 × 2?
items.e: You can multiply in any order. Change the order: 5 × 2 = 10, then 10 × 17 = 170. Multiply all three numbers, not just two.

items.q: Multiply by 10, then halve, to find 46 × 5.
items.e: × 5 is the same as × 10, then halve. 46 × 10 = 460. Half of 460 = 230.

items.q: What is 16 × 25? (Hint: halve one number and double the other.)
items.e: Halve 16 and double 25: 16 × 25 = 8 × 50 = 4 × 100 = 400. If you double one number you must halve the other.

items.q: What is 2 × 36 × 5?

items.q: What is 25 × 4 × 9?

items.q: What is 70 × 80?

items.q: What is 50 × 8?
items.e: 50 is 5 tens. 5 × 8 = 40, so 5 tens × 8 = 40 tens = 400. The 0 in 40 is part of the fact, so do not drop it.

items.q: What is 400 × 6?
items.e: 400 is 4 hundreds. 4 × 6 = 24, so 4 hundreds × 6 = 24 hundreds = 2,400.

items.q: What is 99 × 7?

items.e: 120 is 10 times 12, so the answer is 10 times 108: 1,080.

items.q: What is 900 × 8?
items.e: 900 is 9 hundreds. 9 × 8 = 72, so 9 hundreds × 8 = 72 hundreds = 7,200.

items.q: Double, then double again, to find 37 × 4.
items.e: × 4 is double, double. Double 37 = 74. Double 74 = 148. Doubling only once gives 74; three times gives 296.

items.q: What is 3,000 × 7?
items.e: 3,000 is 3 thousands. 3 × 7 = 21, so 3 thousands × 7 = 21 thousands = 21,000.

items.q: What is 4 × 19 × 25?
items.e: You can multiply in any order. Change the order: 4 × 25 = 100, then 100 × 19 = 1,900. Multiply all three numbers, not just two.

items.q: What is 18 × 50?
items.e: × 50 is the same as × 100, then halve. 18 × 100 = 1,800. Half of 1,800 = 900.

items.q: What is 60 × 7?
items.e: 60 is 6 tens. 6 × 7 = 42, so 6 tens × 7 = 42 tens = 420.

sets.title: Word problems: rates, scaling and two steps

items.q: A train travels 125 km every hour. How far does it travel in 3 hours?
items.e: Equal groups: 3 hours × 125 km, so multiply 125 × 3. Ones: 5 × 3 = 15. Write 5, exchange 1. Tens: 2 × 3 + 1 = 7. Write 7. Hundreds: 1 × 3 = 3. Write 3. Answer: 375.

items.q: A school buys 28 reading books at £7 each and 3 dictionaries at £15 each. What is the total cost?
A box holds 144 pencils. The school office orders 23 boxes. How many pencils is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 23 boxes × 144 pencils, so multiply 144 × 23. Row 1: 144 × 3 = 432. Row 2: 144 × 20 = 2,880 (write the place-holder 0, then 144 × 2 = 288). Add: 432 + 2,880 = 3,312.

items.q: A crate holds 24 bottles of milk. The school orders 35 crates this term. How many bottles is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 35 crates × 24 bottles, so multiply 24 × 35. Row 1: 24 × 5 = 120. Row 2: 24 × 30 = 720 (write the place-holder 0, then 24 × 3 = 72). Add: 120 + 720 = 840.

items.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 175 g of flour. How much flour is needed for 12 people?
items.e: 12 people is 3 times as many as 4 people (4 × 3 = 12), so use 3 times as much flour: 175 × 3 = 525 g. Do not multiply by 12: the recipe is for 4 people, not 1.

items.q: A lorry carries 32 crates. Each crate has a mass of 145 kg. What is the total mass of the crates?
items.e: Equal groups: 32 crates × 145 kg, so multiply 145 × 32. Row 1: 145 × 2 = 290. Row 2: 145 × 30 = 4,350 (write the place-holder 0, then 145 × 3 = 435). Add: 290 + 4,350 = 4,640.

items.q: A school books 6 coaches with 49 seats each. 250 pupils and 22 adults go on the trip. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Step 1: seats: 6 × 49 = 294 (9 × 6 = 54, write 4, exchange 5; 4 × 6 + 5 = 29). Step 2: people: 250 + 22 = 272. Step 3: empty seats: 294 − 272 = 22.

items.q: A bakery bakes 2,350 bread rolls every day. How many rolls does it bake in 6 days?
items.e: Equal groups: 6 days × 2,350 rolls, so multiply 2,350 × 6. Ones: 0 × 6 = 0. Write 0. Tens: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, exchange 3. Hundreds: 3 × 6 + 3 = 21. Write 1, exchange 2. Thousands: 2 × 6 + 2 = 14. Write 14. Answer: 14,100.

items.q: A school trip costs £8 for each pupil. 316 pupils go. How much money is collected?
items.e: Equal groups: 316 pupils × £8, so multiply 316 × 8. Ones: 6 × 8 = 48. Write 8, exchange 4. Tens: 1 × 8 + 4 = 12. Write 2, exchange 1. Hundreds: 3 × 8 + 1 = 25. Write 25. Answer: 2,528.

items.q: A dripping tap wastes 45 ml of water every hour. How much water does it waste in 24 hours?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 hours × 45 ml, so multiply 45 × 24. Row 1: 45 × 4 = 180. Row 2: 45 × 20 = 900 (write the place-holder 0, then 45 × 2 = 90). Add: 180 + 900 = 1,080.

items.q: A gardener is paid £12 an hour. She works for 15 hours this week. How much does she earn?
items.e: Equal groups: 15 hours × £12, so multiply 12 × 15. Row 1: 12 × 5 = 60. Row 2: 12 × 10 = 120 (write the place-holder 0, then 12 × 1 = 12). Add: 60 + 120 = 180.

items.q: Freya cycles 18 km every day for 14 days. How far does she cycle altogether?
items.e: Equal groups: 14 days × 18 km, so multiply 18 × 14. Row 1: 18 × 4 = 72. Row 2: 18 × 10 = 180 (write the place-holder 0, then 18 × 1 = 18). Add: 72 + 180 = 252.

items.q: A glass holds 250 ml. A jug holds 6 times as much. How much does the jug hold?
items.e: 6 times as much, so 250 ml × 6: 250 × 6. Ones: 0 × 6 = 0. Write 0. Tens: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, exchange 3. Hundreds: 2 × 6 + 3 = 15. Write 15. Answer: 1,500.

items.q: A swimming coach is paid £45 an hour. He teaches for 26 hours this half-term. How much is he paid?
items.e: Equal groups: 26 hours × £45, so multiply 45 × 26. Row 1: 45 × 6 = 270. Row 2: 45 × 20 = 900 (write the place-holder 0, then 45 × 2 = 90). Add: 270 + 900 = 1,170.

items.q: A theatre sells 1,236 tickets for a show at £15 each. How much money does it take?
A printer prints 36 pages a minute. How many pages does it print in 25 minutes?
items.e: Equal groups: 25 minutes × 36 pages, so multiply 36 × 25. Row 1: 36 × 5 = 180. Row 2: 36 × 20 = 720 (write the place-holder 0, then 36 × 2 = 72). Add: 180 + 720 = 900.

items.q: The school hall has 27 rows of chairs with 18 chairs in each row. How many chairs are there?
items.e: Equal groups: 27 rows × 18 chairs, so multiply 27 × 18. Row 1: 27 × 8 = 216. Row 2: 27 × 10 = 270 (write the place-holder 0, then 27 × 1 = 27). Add: 216 + 270 = 486.

items.q: A rabbit has a mass of 2,400 g. A guinea pig is 14 as heavy. What is the mass of the guinea pig?
items.e: “14 as heavy” means divide into 4 equal parts: 2,400 ÷ 4 = 600 g. Multiplying by 4 gives 9,600 g, which is heavier, not lighter.

items.q: Ethan says 286 × 34 = 2,002. Estimate to check. Is his answer sensible?
items.e: 286 rounds to 300 and 34 rounds to 30. 300 × 30 = 9,000. 2,002 is far from 9,000, so it cannot be right. Ethan forgot the place-holder 0 in the second row. The correct answer is 9,724.

items.q: A family uses 165 litres of water a day. How much water do they use in a week?
items.e: Equal groups: 7 days × 165 litres, so multiply 165 × 7. Ones: 5 × 7 = 35. Write 5, exchange 3. Tens: 6 × 7 + 3 = 45. Write 5, exchange 4. Hundreds: 1 × 7 + 4 = 11. Write 11. Answer: 1,155.
